# New-ZbxToken

## SYNOPSIS

Creates an API token.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxToken [[-Name] <string>] [-Description <string>] [-UserId <ulong>] [-Status <ZabbixAuthenticationToken>] [-ExpiresAt <DateTimeOffset>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Generate] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An API token logs a user in to the API without a password; it is created without its secret, which the server generates once (token.generate). The New-ZbxToken cmdlet sends token.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new API token back with token.get and writes it. The server requires -Name; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create an API token

```powershell
New-ZbxToken -Name 'Inventory script' -Description 'Read-only access for the inventory script'
```

Writes the new token (token.create, read back with token.get). It belongs to the calling user unless -UserId names another, and it has no secret yet: the server generates one only on request.

### Example 2: Create a token and connect with it

```powershell
$created = New-ZbxToken -Name 'Inventory reader' -Generate
Connect-ZbxServer -Uri 'https://zabbix.example/api_jsonrpc.php' -ApiToken $created.Secret -Name 'inventory' -NoDefault
Get-ZbxApiVersion -Connection 'inventory'
Disconnect-ZbxServer -Name 'inventory'
```

-Generate also asks the server for the token's secret (token.generate) and adds it to the written token as the SecureString property Secret, which Connect-ZbxServer -ApiToken takes as it is. The server shows a secret only this once: keep it (a secret vault, or Export-Clixml, which encrypts it for this user on Windows).

### -Generate

Also generates each new token's secret (token.generate) and adds it to the written token as the property Secret, a SecureString that Connect-ZbxServer -ApiToken takes as it is. The server answers the secret this once and cannot show it again: keep it (a secret vault, or Export-Clixml). It is never written to a stream, a log or an error.

## INPUTS

- `string`: Bound to -Name (ByPropertyName), -Description (ByPropertyName). Text.
- `ulong`: Bound to -UserId (ByPropertyName).
- `ZabbixAuthenticationToken`: Bound to -Status (ByPropertyName). The authentication token values: ZBX_AUTH_TOKEN_* in defines.inc.php.
- `DateTimeOffset`: Bound to -ExpiresAt (ByPropertyName).
- `PSObject`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Each object as the API answers it.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixToken`: Token class.
